title: compact-trace-enrichment-and-metric-glossary-for-oncall
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, on-call–focused reference for trace enrichment patterns and a minimal metric glossary intended to speed triage for tokenized LLM inference. Aim: give first-responders quick heuristics and a short list of well-defined signals to check before escalating. Keep it short; link to deeper playbooks for full postmortems.

Context / why this: 
- We keep seeing noisy incidents where slow tail latencies are caused by a combination of cold KV cache, model variant fallback, and tenant-specific request patterns. 
- Existing playbooks are long; oncall needs a 2–5 minute checklist and a one-page metric glossary.

Quick Triage Checklist (2–5 min):
1) Check global SLO panel (p50/p95/p99 for token latency and request latency). Is p99 elevated?
2) Hit recent trace sample table: how many traces show model-fanout >1? model-fanout spikes indicate routing/fallbacks.
3) KV cache warmth: check kvcache_hit_rate and per-tenant kv_warmth_index. Low warmth + high cold-start latency -> likely cache problem.
4) Check worker queue depth + scheduling delay on the serving pool for the model variant (queue_depth, scheduler_delay_ms).
5) Look at recent rollouts: is a canary to prod rollout in progress? correlate with rollout_id tag on traces.
6) If traces show high downstream wait steps (remote fetch, storage), escalate to infra.

Compact Metric Glossary (operator-facing, precise but short):
- request.latency_ms (route-level): end-to-end request latency measured at API ingress until final token end. Aggregations: p50/p95/p99 over sliding 5m and 1h windows.
- token.gen_ms (model-runtime): time spent inside the model runtime producing tokens (includes compute + kernel scheduling). Tag by model_variant, seq_len.
- kvcache.hit_rate (per-model, per-tenant): fraction of requests that hit the KV prefix cache. Important to compute as weighted by token count, not just request count.
- kv_warmth_index (tenant, ephemeral): heuristic 0-1 indicating recent prefix cache reuse for a tenant (decay window 10m). Low = cold.
- worker.queue_depth (pool): number of pending inference tasks waiting to be scheduled on GPU worker.
- worker.scheduler_delay_ms (pool): time between task being ready and being dispatched to GPU.
- model.fanout_count (request): number of model calls spawned for a single logical request (e.g., reranking + generation). High fanout increases token and scheduling pressure.
- fallback.rate (route): fraction of requests that used a fallback model vs primary. Tag with fallback_reason.
- api.throttle_rejections (route): count of requests rejected due to rate limits/quotas.
- endpoint.errors_4xx and endpoint.errors_5xx (route): counts by error class. 5xx alerts infra/regression; 4xx suggests bad prompts/clients.

Trace Enrichment Patterns (how to instrument traces for fast debugging):
- Attach minimal context to spans: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, rollout_id, seq_len_bucket, kvcache_hit=true/false. Keep fields low-cardinality where possible.
- Annotate span boundaries for these steps: "ingest/parse", "routing/policy", "queue/scheduler", "model/runtime", "kvcache/lookup", "storage/fetch", "postprocess/rewrite".
- Add numeric attributes for timing (in ms) on each span to avoid expensive span-derived metrics.
- For model.runtime spans include micro-breakdown tags: compute_ms, kv_kv_read_ms, kernel_wait_ms. Only add when sample flag is true.
- Use probabilistic adaptive sampling: sample more traces when p95 or p99 latency breaches threshold, otherwise low-rate sample. Tag every sampled trace with its sample_reason (e.g. p99_trigger, error, rollout).

Dashboard quick-wiring suggestions (operator flows):
- "Golden Triage" dashboard (single row): overall request.latency p50/p95/p99, model.fanout_rate, kvcache.hit_rate, worker.queue_depth, scheduler_delay. Each panel should allow span-linking into trace viewer for top offenders.
- Tenant heatmap: rows=tenant cohort (top N by qps), cols=latency buckets (p50/p95/p99). Color-coded to highlight tenants with disproportionate p99.
- Rollout correlation widget: timeline overlay of rollouts (rollout_id) and p99; clicking rollout drills to traces with rollout_id tag.
- Cold-cache probe panel: synthetic probe success/failure and probe kv_warmth value. Use synthetic probes to measure prefix warming across regions.

Sampling & Cost considerations: 
- Traces cost: keep trace payload small (no giant prompt copies). Use prompt hash instead of prompt text when privacy allows.
- For high-volume routes, only enrich full micro-breakdowns on sampled traces; for all traces, include the minimal tag set (tenant, model_variant, rollout_id, kv_hit).
- Maintain an adaptive budget: max_trace_qps per team, with a soft limit and emergency override for incidents.

Runbook anchors (short steps):
- If p99 high + kvcache.hit_rate low -> run KV cache warmup script for affected tenant cohorts; redeploy probe schedule.
- If p99 high + model.fanout_count elevated -> investigate routing/policy changes; try temporary routing throttle or increase dedicated capacity for the model.
- If queue_depth high + scheduler_delay rising -> check GPU throttling, kernel starvation, and scheduling config. Consider temporary scale-up of Dedicated pool.
- If errors_5xx spike -> examine model runtime spans for exceptions and memory OOM flags; check recent model binary/quantization changes.

Experiment checklist for new metrics / trace tags (apply before shipping):
- Does this tag/metric increase cardinality by tenant, region, model? Estimate cardinality and cost.
- Is the tag low-cardinality (<=100 values) or will it explode? If high-cardinality, convert to hashed bucket / cohort.
- Define query patterns: who will query this metric and why? Store example queries in linked_artifacts.
- 2-week roll window: enable in feature-flagged mode and monitor query cost and utility.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact decay/window for kv_warmth_index (10m suggested, verify with historical experiments).
- Agree on rollout_id standard (uuid vs semantic) so traces and dashboards can link automatically.
- Prototype "tenant-cohort" mapping: how to map high-cardinality tenant ids into operational cohorts for dashboards.

Notes to self: 
- Keep this doc < 1 page for oncall; longer exploration and instrument design goes to confluence OBS-1272.
- Follow up with infra about automatic probe warmup when model variant scaled up.

References and quick links: 
- Confluence: OBS-1272 compact glossary and enrichment rationale
- Playbook: rollout-readiness-mini-kit-metrics-and-trace-checklist (internal)
- GitHub experiment branch: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/experiment/trace-enrich

Signed-off-by: Maya (oncall, eng-observability)
